$comment: Declaration of every PR-reachable CI job in this repository.
WHY THIS EXISTS: CI jobs accrete one unremarkable job at a time, and without a
declaration nothing says anything at the moment each is added. This file makes
adding a job a DECLARED ACT rather than a silent one. It is a METER, not a cure:
it measures and names the footprint, it does not reduce it.
CAPACITY MODEL — the deliberate divergence from the originating repo.
The upstream artifact set (kailash-rs, loom#1877) models pools with fixed
capacities because it runs on a self-hosted fleet where 33 jobs against a pool
of 24 is a real exhaustion. THIS repo runs entirely on GitHub-hosted runners,
which are elastic and billed rather than pooled, so a capacity ceiling would be
a number with no referent. Inventing one would be worse than omitting it: the
gate would compare demand against a fiction and report a green that means
nothing. So the capacity half is NOT adopted, and this gate checks DECLARATION
COMPLETENESS instead — every PR-reachable job must be accounted for.
The spend axis is owned separately by rules/ci-cost-discipline.md.
DISPOSITIONS (exactly one per job):
required         - a branch-protection required status context; gates merges.
relevance_gated  - carries a job-level `if:` or a trigger-level paths filter,
so it does not fire on PRs it cannot be relevant to.
budgeted         - neither of the above, but explicitly accepted. REQUIRES a
dated rationale; the audit rejects a budgeted entry without
one, so this cannot become a silent catch-all.
capacity_note: No fixed pool. This gate does not compare demand against a capacity ceiling; see $comment.

required_contexts_source.note: Branch protection is MUTABLE repo state. Re-measure rather than citing this block; the audit reads THIS file, so a drifted protection setting shows up as a stale declaration, not as a silently-passing gate.

jobs.rationale: The merge gate. Structure, image-pin consistency, cross-reference ratchet, undeclared-surface hard gate.
Job-level `if:` skips metadata-only release/* branches, so a version bump does not pay a container build.
Job-level `if:` restricts it to the auto-merge path; it is a notification, not a gate.
